name: classifications
description: The four NADDP data classification zones. See docs/architecture/adr/0006-classification-zones.md for the full rules. rank is the DOMINANCE order used for propagation: any aggregate, summary, AI output or evidence list takes the maximum rank of its constituent parts. min_role_rank_to_read plus compartment is the ACCESS rule; the two are deliberately separate, because CONSULAR_SENSITIVE is a compartment (need-to-know about a private individual) rather than simply a higher tier. Identifiers use underscores; BUILD_BIBLE.md section 5 writes them with hyphens as display labels only.

role_ranks.description: Head of mission; accountable for everything the mission does.
Acts for the Ambassador and needs equivalent reach.
Working tier plus the consular compartment. Deliberately not rank 30: a consular officer's need-to-know is deep, not broad.
Full working access to trade and intelligence material; no consular need-to-know.
Working tier. Diaspora profiles are governed by consent rather than by the consular compartment.
Platform administration and audit reading. Explicitly NOT a content super-user - separation of duties (ADR-0003).

classifications.label: Public
classifications.description: Already published, or intended for publication. Disclosure causes no harm because it has already occurred. The only zone permitted on the unauthenticated citizen surface.
classifications.example_content: A cited public agency page underpinning an intelligence signal; published trade statistics; a public university programme description; the citizen-facing explanation of how to renew a passport.

classifications.label: Mission Internal
classifications.description: Ordinary working material of the mission. Not secret, but not for publication; disclosure is embarrassing and erodes working candour. The default zone for anything a staff member authors and for any newly ingested material outside a consular context.
classifications.example_content: A draft morning brief; internal notes on an opportunity's scoring rationale; a stakeholder contact record; a meeting agenda; the mission's own commentary on a public source.

classifications.label: Consular Sensitive
classifications.description: Personal information about identifiable individuals in a consular context. Distinguished from CONFIDENTIAL not by how damaging disclosure would be in diplomatic terms, but by WHOSE interests are harmed - a private person's, who did not choose to be in the system. Requires the consular compartment in addition to rank, so seniority alone never opens a case file.
classifications.example_content: A passport renewal case file; a welfare or detention matter; next-of-kin details; case correspondence; any document attached to a consular case.

classifications.label: Confidential
classifications.description: Material whose disclosure would damage the bilateral relationship or a commercial party. Highest dominance rank, so anything derived from it is also CONFIDENTIAL. Officers below rank 30 who need access receive an explicit, audited per-object grant rather than a blanket clearance.
classifications.example_content: A negotiating position on a lithium value-chain agreement; an unannounced commercial intention shared in confidence; a candid political assessment; third-party commercially-confidential information.

access_rule: may_read(principal, zone) := (principal.clearance_rank >= zone.min_role_rank_to_read AND (zone.compartment is null OR zone.compartment in principal.compartments)) OR an explicit, audited per-object grant exists for (principal, object). Propagation uses rank alone: derived content takes max(rank) over its parts, and downgrade is always a deliberate, audited human act.
